public_rationale: The claim attributes an undefined investment 'bubble' to Altman's persuasion and contrasts it with an undefined personal quality, 'super-genius' [wyea-the-openai-bubble-0cd71a-o1]. This wording provides no measurable outcome or test that separates the proposed causes [wyea-the-openai-bubble-0cd71a-o1]. SoftBank's April 1, 2025 disclosure links its investment decision to model advancement, computing needs and expected benefits from OpenAI's growth [e1]. That disclosure records one investor's stated reasons. It cannot settle the claim's exclusive causal contrast [e1].
limitations: The claim defines no valuation benchmark, magnitude or period for the bubble.
The evidence does not isolate persuasion from technical progress, business ability or other investment motives.
The claim supplies no testable counterfactual. Not adjudicable does not mean false.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The OpenAI bubble inflated because Sam Altman tells people what they want to hear, not because of genius.

statement.excerpt: The OpenAI Bubble inflated not because Sam Altman is a super-genius, but because he’s very, very good at telling people what they want to hear.

from_speaker: not because Sam Altman is a super-genius
because he’s very, very good at telling people what they want to hear
our_interpretation: The sentence offers an exclusive causal contrast between persuasive appeals and an undefined personal quality.
Fundraising records and investor explanations can test whether expectations influenced investment. They cannot, by themselves, establish the stated contrast with genius.
Replacing 'bubble' with investment growth and 'super-genius' with a measurable business capability would materially rewrite the claim.
criteria.support_condition: No fair operational condition is available as written. A testable version would need a defined investment outcome, defined competing causes and evidence separating their contributions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No fair operational condition is available as written. Evidence of technical progress or investor enthusiasm alone cannot refute the asserted personal and causal contrast.
